channel.title: Global Arbitration Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Arbitration Review (globalarbitrationreview.com)

item.title: Lalive advises Montenegro on road dispute
item.description: Montenegro has turned to Lalive for a dispute with a Chinese state-owned construction company over a controversial toll road project.

item.title: Lukoil threatens Bulgaria over seized assets
item.description: A subsidiary of Russia’s Lukoil has threatened to bring an ICSID claim against Bulgaria after the state put its assets into administration to avoid a fuel crisis caused by US sanctions.

item.title: ECJ advocate general says sanctions disputes are arbitrable
item.description: An advocate general of the European Court of Justice has advised that contractual claims caught by the EU’s Russia sanctions regulation are capable of being arbitrated, while stating that the prohibition on satisfying such claims forms part of EU public policy.

item.title: GAR Live considers Riyadh's potential as regional hub
item.description: A session at GAR Live Riyadh considered whether the "future-minded" Saudi Arabian capital could be the next leading regional arbitration hub and what it has to do to build its arbitration ecosystem further.

item.title: HKIAC panel orders Chinese education group to proceed with buyout
item.description: An HKIAC tribunal has ruled that Hong Kong-listed Minsheng Education Group must proceed with a US$315 million buyout of its partners in a Cayman entity that operates schools and colleges in China.

item.title: Cayman fund fails to block LCIA claim over alleged mismanagement
item.description: The Cayman Islands Court of Appeal has upheld a stay of litigation pending an LCIA case over alleged mismanagement of an investment fund that holds a valuable stake in a Pakistani power utility – an asset that is also the subject of a US$2 billion investment treaty claim.

item.title: Hong Kong court halts bribery claim in Congo mining saga
item.description: A Hong Kong court has restrained a Chinese state-owned entity from pursuing a new HKIAC claim against London-based commodities trader Gerald Group over alleged bribery – finding it was a collateral attack on awards already issued in a long-running arbitration.

item.title: Romania loses state aid challenge to OMV award
item.description: The Paris Court of Appeal has upheld a €59 million ICC award won by Austrian oil and gas group OMV against Romania over environmental clean-up costs, rejecting the state’s arguments that it amounted to unlawful state aid.

item.title: Canadian mining investor seeks to enforce against Peru
item.description: A Canadian mining company has asked a US court to enforce an ICSID award requiring Peru to pay US$68 million over the seizure of a mine by members of a rural community.

item.title: UK court enforces US$66 billion Yukos awards
item.description: The Commercial Court in London has allowed the former majority shareholders of Yukos Oil Company to enforce Energy Charter Treaty awards worth more than US$66 billion against Russia, dismissing the state’s arguments that the awards were procured through fraud.
